referents.why: third masculine singular 'his' on 'steadfast love'; the only agreeing sensible possessor is the LORD, whom the first clause names and the following kî-clauses describe ('He is good')
referents.category: possessive pronoun resolved to the subject of the preceding reason clause

referents.why: second masculine plural imperative 'give thanks'; the verse names no audience and no candidate (LORD, forever, steadfast love, the psalmist voice) can be the ones commanded; the psalmist is not addressed by his own call to others
referents.category: implied addressee of an opening command with no named audience

links.why: the opening kî after an imperative gives the ground for the command: give thanks, for he is good
the second kî is a parallel reason, not a reason for 'he is good'; the two kî-clauses are coordinate grounds for the same command
links.category: coordinate reason clauses read as a chain

links.why: the second kî-clause ('his loyal love is forever') is a second reason for the command to give thanks, parallel to cl1
links.category: coordinate reason clauses read as a chain

groups.why: 'part' is not a role of an imperative; the two kî-clauses are the grounds (basis) of the command
groups.category: reason clauses filed under the wrong imperative role

groups.why: the verse has no heading or ascription, so cl0 is not a frame; the LORD is the object of thanks, not the writer, so he is not the sender; the verse's content is the commanded call with its grounds, held as imp0 (cl1 and cl2 are inside it)
groups.category: wrong role assigned to a command and a named deity in a unit

cant_tell.why: the verse names no writer and has no first-person voice, so the writing has no sender

cant_tell.what: the audience called to give thanks
cant_tell.why: no audience is named in this verse and no candidate stands for the people addressed
